dataset.name: Mozilla CORE
dataset.target: first valid P1-P5 Priority assigned strictly after Creation and within following 24 hours

final_model.name: TF-IDF + Class-Weighted Logistic Regression
final_model.selection_basis: validation macro-F1 with minority-class performance considered

system_role.description: T2 is suitable as a secondary, confidence-aware priority prediction signal within the integrated IT Ticket Intelligence system. It should assist triage and downstream evidence fusion, but should not independently determine final ticket priority.

strengths: The T2 target has an explicit temporal definition: first valid P1-P5 Priority assigned after Creation and within the following 24 hours.
The prediction boundary is Creation, preserving the intended incoming-ticket decision boundary.
The modeling features are restricted to Creation-time Summary and Description.
A chronological train/validation/test split was used.
The locked test set was evaluated only after model selection.
The final evaluation was performed without retraining or refitting.
The model provides measurable signal for priority prediction, especially for the more represented classes.
limitations: Overall five-class predictive performance is limited: final test accuracy is 42.0113% and macro-F1 is 26.4960%.
Minority-class performance is very weak, with P4 F1=4.1237% and P5 F1=6.7340%.
Performance decreases from validation to the later locked test period.
The dominant error paths involve confusion among P1, P2, and P3.
The evidence does not justify treating the model as a fully autonomous priority assignment system.
A universal automated confidence threshold has not been empirically established.
supported_claims: A leakage-controlled five-class priority prediction experiment can be performed on Mozilla CORE.
Creation-time Summary and Description contain predictive signal for the subsequent 24-hour priority outcome.
The selected model generalizes to a later chronological test period, although with degraded performance.
Priority prediction is substantially harder for P4 and P5 than for the more represented priority classes.
T2 can contribute one evidence channel to a larger confidence-aware triage system.
unsupported_claims: T2 does not support claiming highly accurate autonomous five-class priority assignment.
T2 does not support claiming reliable prediction of P4 or P5.
T2 does not support automatic action at a fixed confidence threshold without further empirical calibration and policy evaluation.
T2 does not establish that predicted priority should replace human priority judgment.
final_conclusion: Mozilla CORE is suitable for T2 priority-prediction modeling under the frozen Creation-time target and feature boundary. The final TF-IDF + Class-Weighted Logistic Regression model demonstrates measurable but limited predictive performance on the locked chronological test period. Because minority-class performance is weak and generalization degrades on the later period, T2 is closed as a supported secondary decision-support signal rather than an autonomous priority assignment component.
next_system_use: Retain the T2 prediction as one evidence channel for later confidence-aware fusion and human-review policy development. Do not independently automate final priority assignment from T2.
